caption: I had wanted to do something image-wise for Domestic Abuse Awareness Month. I mean, no doubt, I think we're all . . . aware. I've been fiddling with the phrase domestic abuse, and I must say, COVID-45 has totally stretched, filled, apotheosed, epitomized, gold-boilerplated the true spirit of the phrase. Domestic as in the household, but also in the borders of the nation. Ass Above, So Below Me. And read aloud to yourself the White House statement for Domestic Abuse Awareness Month and file it under Stole Wallet, Coordinated the Search. For the past couple weeks I was flippantly engaging with an AI to do a cheeky love story about 45 that was inspired by astrological app on my phone. After a couple dozen iterations, it was not wanting to go that way. So early yesterday, I fed a scenario within AI Dungeon which employs the GPT-3 Natural Language Processing Thingamajig, I added to its world info the idea of a perpetrated-perpetrator dichotomy, and as many tactics of deflection, manipulation, and other behaviors employed by 45 and the folks who have been empowered by him the past four years. It's an attempt at a working within dynamic fictional realms to improve our chances of a smooth divorce as a nation. For most of it, i've been using the dictation function which I never use, so you'll know who wrote what by the lack of commas. I got a bunch of scenes that seem to have curious overlapping themes, i'll try to do one a day so there may be thirty-one chapters. And I'm using Microsoft's Immersive Reader which has impressive reading voices so that the text can be put in the background as folk go about preparing for whatever's coming. When I cope, I cope big. This is a long fucker at 24 min, hoping to make things briefer but I wanted to show the process of the AI seeming to acclimate to conditions, this is what I've been waiting for my whole life, since talking to Eliza who in the AppleIIE was a program called Freud with big bushy eyebrows, who I hope in digital ghost form might want to apologize to the meatspace for denying women's reality and instead suggesting maybe they just weren't having enough sex in their lives. 'Tis the season for thinking of the wars waged at home, and how they've spilt on the streets.
